title: AI intelligence graph
tagline: An expanding understanding of the fast-moving AI world, built from public, private and unique sources. Event attendance is one of them.
healthWhy: At risk because the 16 November test depends on phase 1 work that has started but isn't finished (the nightly checking job and the backfill), and on a scheduled runner that failed its first two test runs. Not off track: the design, the decisions and the pilot evidence are in place, and no target date has moved.
confidence: 60%: moderately confident the 16 November brief ships on phase 1
summary: At risk, and improving. The graph is meant to be an expanding understanding of the AI world drawn from many sources, but only 3 of the 9 source types that have ever fed it are still writing, and even the event record is incomplete: 30 of 85 attended events have their first-hand notes in it. Phase 1 fixes completeness this week with a nightly job that checks every source and fills the gaps, and starts theme-driven web search; the 16 November Monday brief is the test. From Alex it needs one decision below (how private originals are stored), five minutes setting up a machine, one database change applied, and two builds merged.
phase: Phase 1: complete the graph and start the discovery loop
why: AI moves faster than any one person can follow, and the best view of it combines sources nobody else has together. Public sources are the web, news, papers, models, filings, job boards and social. Private ones are newsletters and correspondence, meeting notes, and the insights and review comments in Notion. Unique ones are the rooms Alex is in and what he publishes. The project started as a fix for a silent failure, when topic trends stopped absorbing new topics on 8 August. A 10 November audit then showed the larger problem. Most sources had gone quiet: 3 of 9 source types still write. Graph writes were the manual last step of long commands, mandatory on paper and never enforced or measured. And the market side polled a fixed list of 40 companies instead of discovering anything.
mission: One knowledge graph that keeps growing from every useful source, read through lenses (attended, research, market, job) and sliceable by theme, company, segment and time. Each source arrives through a 'lane': a scheduled job with a run log, an alarm, a reader and a kill rule. A nightly checking job compares every source against the graph and fills the gaps through one guarded writer. A discovery loop lets rising themes and each week's events choose what to search for, across web search, connectors like Clay, newsletters and social. It checks what was said in the room against what the market says, and counts every reuse of a fact.
destination: Every source that's worth having feeds the graph on a schedule, with a completeness score and an alarm. Before any room, conversation or post, the brief says what moved in its themes, which companies and people are new, and where Alex's first-hand view agrees or conflicts with the market. The Monday Market Brief is the weekly proof. The graph is the memory behind content, outreach and the job search.
showcase: Auditing a knowledge graph against its own sources and stating each gap as a dated count before proposing a fix
Reconciliation over reminders: a nightly job checks what should exist and fills the gap, instead of hoping each manual step ran (the pattern Kubernetes uses)
A discovery loop: the graph's own trends generate the search questions, read-only agents fetch, and one guarded writer stores the results
Keeping facts honest over time: each new claim is marked as corroborating, refining, replacing or contradicting older ones, and only real conflicts go to a human
The operating rule each lane is held to: a run log, an alarm, a reader and a kill rule. The audit found two lanes breaking it, and fixing them is part of this phase

decisions.decision: Build four lenses with sliceable cohorts instead of one trend view.
decisions.why: Thin data is a reason to ingest more, not to shrink the scope.

decisions.decision: Lane 2 runs on the free stack plus Clay.
decisions.why: It was the only measured option that cleared the recall and coverage floors (0.69 and 0.88).

decisions.decision: Replace list-polling with a discovery loop: rising themes, coverage gaps and each week's events generate the searches, and the watchlist grows on evidence.
decisions.why: Matching a vendor on a fixed list defends coverage that already exists. A read-only pilot found that 34 of 38 companies driving the three fastest-rising themes were missing from the graph.

decisions.decision: Scheduled jobs run the loop. Findings are held in a staging table first, and they're promoted into the graph unattended only after a precision spot-check clears 0.8. The watchlist grows itself, and only contradictions reach Alex.
decisions.why: Anything that depended on a manual trigger has died in this project before. The one gate kept up front is a quality floor on web-derived claims.

decisions.decision: Make the graph complete backwards and self-maintaining forwards, with a completeness score per source.
decisions.why: The audit showed the write steps exist but are skipped silently, so the fix is a reconciler that checks, not a reminder.

decisions.decision: Events that were researched but not attended get their own 'researched' event type, promoted to attended when attendance is confirmed.
decisions.why: About 4,900 research claims had no event to attach to. A separate type keeps them findable without overstating attendance.

decisions.decision: An event counts as attended once its post-event content has been uploaded and Alex has acknowledged it.
decisions.why: That is the strongest evidence available, it already exists for every event that matters, and it needs no extra step.

decisions.decision: A nightly checking job keeps the graph complete: it compares every source against the graph and fills the gaps.
decisions.why: The audit showed the write steps exist but get skipped silently. A job that checks beats a reminder to remember.

risks.risk: Web searches lean on news aggregators, so dates and figures can be wrong.
risks.mitigation: Fetch the original page for every item before it's written. Let the loop write without review only after a spot check shows at least 80% of its findings are right.

risks.risk: The backfill is large, and duplicate companies and people can multiply across sources.
risks.mitigation: Dry-run every batch, map alternate names to one entity, and write everything through the one guarded writer.

risks.risk: The loop could go quiet again the way earlier lanes did.
risks.mitigation: Today's health check flags a lane after 7 quiet days and fails it after 14. Phase 1 tightens daily lanes to 2 and 4.

risks.risk: The Clay credits on hand are limited and will run out after a few runs of the company-news leg.
risks.mitigation: Decide on credits or a plan before they run out. The free sources keep flowing either way.

log.text: Decisions: discovery loop, scheduled routines as the runner, staged writes, autonomous watchlist. Phase 1 is planned to ship this week.
Pilot theme search: 68 dated events and 38 companies across three rising themes, 34 of them new to the graph.
Graph audit: 30 of 85 attended events with first-hand claims, 52 of 97 researched events in the graph, first claim written 18 September.
Decision: lane 2 runs on the free stack plus Clay. The build has started.
Lane 2 bake-off: the free stack plus Clay reached 0.69 recall against akta (floor 0.60) and 0.88 coverage.
Lanes 0 and 3 merged. Lane 4's table and fetcher passed review.
Backlog topics assigned to themes and three themes added.
Gap diagnosed on the live graph and the fix plan written.

asks.decision: Where are private originals stored (email, meeting notes, Notion comments, raw transcripts)?
asks.recommendation: Keep the originals in a separate private vault, encrypted and outside the graph and the public repos, with its own key that no scheduled job or pull request can reach. The graph stores what was learned plus a pointer back to the original, so any source can be mined again as the models improve.
options: Store originals in the graph's own database (one key reaches everything, including from public-repo jobs)
Store only what was learned and discard the originals (lose the ability to re-mine and to quote exactly)
asks.costOfDelay: Email and meeting notes can't join the graph until this is settled. Everything else in phase 1 proceeds.

changes.text: The scope widened from a view of NYC AI rooms to an expanding understanding of the AI world, with event attendance as one source among many.
Audit of the live graph: 30 of 85 attended events have first-hand claims, and 45 of 97 researched events never reached the graph.
A read-only pilot search of three rising themes found 68 dated events and 38 companies, 34 of them new to the graph. This is descriptive; there's no comparison sample yet.
The goal changed from matching a paid vendor on 40 companies to a discovery loop over a complete graph.
Two design reviews written. The runner, the write path and the level of autonomy were decided.
The scheduled runner: two smoke runs couldn't reach the project's Python environment, and runs currently land on a laptop.
The lane 2 build moved from done back to waiting on merge.

issues.issue: Two lanes (hiring and research papers) run every week but write nothing.
issues.impact: Those signals are missing from the market lens, and the health check doesn't count it.
issues.action: Start their writes or retire them on purpose, and count zero-write runs as failures.

issues.issue: Scheduled runs can't reach the project's Python environment, and they run on a laptop that sleeps.
issues.action: Register the always-on machine, have each run set up its own environment, and fall back to a plain scheduled job if that fails.
